topics.label: Course Introduction and Lecture Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer biology course structure, the diverse student backgrounds, and the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cellular, Genetic, and Architectural Basis of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the biological foundation of cancer as a progressive accumulation of genetic changes and a failure of normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Tumor Invasion and Metastatic Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how neoplasms progress from localized benign lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies, illustrated through histological features and the colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Impact
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the classification systems used for neoplasms and the physiological mechanisms through which tumors impair organ function and cause disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative and Population Incidence of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the distribution, frequency, and mortality of various cancer types across human populations and multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the diagnostic principles, methodologies, and clinical effectiveness of population screening programs for detecting tumors at early stages.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of the learning outcomes and reminders for upcoming practical classes.
